scRTtools

Documentation website: https://midimagi.github.io/scRTtools/

Single-cell DNA replication timing (scRT) analysis for 10x multiome data.

scRTtools covers the analysis from genome binning and cell QC to replication states, replication tracks, pseudobulk replication timing, initiation zones, replication tempo and replication-expression statistics. Plotting is not part of the package: every function returns an object (GRanges, matrix, data.frame or list) and writes no files unless that is its stated purpose.

The functions were validated against the in-house analysis code they were derived from: on synthetic inputs for every module, and on the bundled example data (chr1 to chr19, 40 cells) for a 21-step chain that runs from cell QC to the HC3 regressions.

Installation

The package needs R >= 4.1 and a C++ compiler; it is developed and tested with R 4.3.3.

Install from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("midimagi/scRTtools")

or from a local clone of the repository:

R CMD INSTALL scRTtools

To keep a Conda environment untouched, install into a library of your own (R CMD INSTALL -l ~/R/scRTtools-lib scRTtools) and load it with library(scRTtools, lib.loc = "~/R/scRTtools-lib"). During development, devtools::load_all() in the package directory loads the package without installing it.

Dependencies

  • Imports: BiocGenerics, BiocParallel, changepoint, data.table, GenomeInfoDb, GenomicRanges, IRanges, Matrix, Rcpp, rlang, Rsamtools, S4Vectors, withr, zoo, plus the base packages methods, splines, stats, tools and utils.

  • Suggests, each needed by a few functions only and checked when the function is called:

    Package Needed by
    mgcv fit_rep_tempo(model_type = "gam_low" / "gam_fast"), fit_all_izone_velocities, the S-phase progression marker functions
    robustbase, quantreg track length and velocity models (fit_track_velocity_linear, fit_track_length_models, fit_track_velocity_ode)
    rtracklayer annotate_peak_scores, annotate_iz_bigwig, bigWig input in general
    Biostrings GC content in make_fixed_bins
    SeuratObject load_and_merge_rna_counts
    cluster silhouette widths in cluster_iz_heterogeneity
    DNAcopy annotate_track_segments
    RhpcBLASctl limits BLAS threads inside parallel fit_rep_tempo workers

  • downsample_fragments() runs the bundled shell script inst/scripts/downsample_fragments_fast.sh and needs bgzip and tabix on the PATH.

Getting started 

library(scRTtools)

ex <- scrt_example_data()   # sample scRT1, chr1-chr19, 12 G1 + 28 S-phase cells
names(ex)

vignette("scRTtools")       # the whole workflow on the example data

The vignette runs the pipeline end to end on the example data and shows the object each step returns.

Overview of the workflow 

genome            make_fixed_bins -> compute_bin_mappability
                         |
per sample        count_reads / filter_windows -> calculate_mapd -> find_g1_cells
                  -> define_G1_windows -> synchronize_bins (across samples)
                  (optional) optimize_shrink_factor -> downsample_fragments
                         |
states            assign_replication_states (HMM: infer_single_cell_states)
                  -> compute_rep_percent
                  (tuning) evaluate_state_parameters -> rank_state_parameters
                         |
tracks            define_replication_tracks -> calc_rep_track_lengths / _gaps
                  -> summarize_track_lengths -> fit_track_velocity_linear / _ode
                         |
pseudobulk RT     calculate_pseudobulk_rt -> find_rt_peaks -> annotate_peak_scores
                  (S/G1 ratio variant: aggregate_pseudobulk_s_g1_counts ->
                   calculate_pseudobulk_rt_g1_ratio; export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio does both)
                  count_track_centers
                         |
initiation zones  define_initiation_zones -> calculate_firing_range
                  -> calculate_firing_order / predict_firing_order
                  -> fit_all_izone_velocities, adjacent-zone statistics,
                     zone heterogeneity (usage, tensor, clustering, CP, epigenome)
                         |
tempo             rep_tempo -> fit_rep_tempo (sslogis / gam_low / gam_fast)
                         |
RNA               SC2P_gene_unit, gex_tempo, S-phase progression markers
                         |
statistics        group comparison (pivot_state_wide ... call_diff_groups),
                  HC3 regressions (fit_ols_hc3, fit_poisson_hc3,
                  combine_two_samples, permute_within_bins)

Conventions used throughout:

  • Bins and windows are GRanges; per-cell tracks are a GRangesList or a list of GRanges.
  • State matrices are bins x cells with copy-number states 2 (unreplicated) and 4 (replicated), NA where no call was made.
  • Functions that loop over cells take BPPARAM (default BiocParallel::SerialParam()).
  • Functions that draw random numbers take seed.
  • Progress messages are controlled by verbose, which defaults to FALSE everywhere; pass verbose = TRUE to see progress of the long-running steps (counting, G1 calling, state inference, tracks, initiation zones).

Not included: plotting, the Seurat WNN/UMAP workflow (standard Seurat steps; the vignette shows how Seurat objects connect to the package) and transcriptional bursting models.

Defaults worth knowing

  • fit_rep_tempo: n_boot defaults to 0; bootstrap confidence intervals (e.g. n_boot = 200) take hours genome-wide.
  • assign_replication_states uses infer_args = list(hmm_aggr_width = 15, init_ratio_lower = 1.2, final_ratio_lower = 1.4); tune these on new data with evaluate_state_parameters.
  • define_G1_windows(min.gapwidth = 100000) and define_initiation_zones(min_usage = 3) are tuned for 20 kb bins and a few hundred cells per sample; lower min_usage for small datasets.
  • fit_ols_hc3: a fit whose largest leverage reaches max_leverage = 0.99 returns NA with status = "high_leverage"; pass Inf to never reject a fit.
  • combine_two_samples: with failed = "keep" failed fits stay in the result (p = 1, status = "fit_failed") and count in later multiple-testing corrections; "drop" removes them.
  • Group comparison functions take states = c("ctr", "ama"); set them to your own condition names.

Development 

devtools::document()
devtools::test()
devtools::check()               # R CMD check --as-cran, builds the vignette

A few tests compare the package with the original in-house code and a real-data regression reference. These files are not part of the repository; the tests find them through environment variables (see tests/testthat/helper-local-paths.R) and skip when the variables are unset, as on GitHub Actions. data-raw/ holds the scripts that build the example data and the regression reference.
